title: Forgive Us for Thy Mercy's Sake
description: Forgive Us for Thy Mercy's Sake in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 325 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Imploring Forgiveness and Renewal of Heart”, where the book credits them to Wesley's Collection.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: For-give us for thy mer-cy's sake; Our mul-ti-tude of sins for-give; And for thy own pos-ses-sion take, And bid us to thy glo-ry live; Live in thy sight and glad-ly prove Our faith by our obe-di-ent love.

lines: Forgive us for thy mercy's sake;
And for thy own possession take,
And bid us to thy glory live;
Live in thy sight and gladly prove
Our faith by our obedient love.
And all thy mighty wonders show;
And conquering them to conquer go,
Till all of pride and wrath be slain,
And not one evil thought remain.
O, put it in our inward parts
The living law of perfect love:
Write the new precept on our hearts;
We shall not then from thee remove,
Who in thy glorious image shine,

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
